source.title: Some Recent Results and Open Problems on Sets of Lengths of Krull Monoids with Finite Class Group

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group with |G| at least 3 and invariant-factor decomposition G ≅ C_{n1} ⊕ ... ⊕ C_{nr}, where C_n is a cyclic group of order n and 1 < n1 | ... | nr. For the monoid B(G) of zero-sum sequences over G, let Delta(G) denote the set of all positive gaps between consecutive lengths that occur in sets of factorization lengths of elements of B(G). Must the largest such distance satisfy max Delta(G) = max{nr - 2, -1 + sum_{i=1}^r floor(ni/2)}?
accepted.context_brief: maximum distance in sets of lengths

evidence.quote: Let A ⊂ Z. Then the set of distances of A, denoted by ∆(A), is the set of all differences between consecutive elements of A
Problem 5.7. Let G ∼= Cn1 ⊕ · · · ⊕ Cnr with |G| ≥ 3 and 1 < n1 | · · · | nr . Is max ∆(G) = max{nr − 2, −1 + sum floor(ni/2)}?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group and let B(G) be the monoid of zero-sum sequences over G. For an element a of B(G), let L(a) be the set of all possible numbers of irreducible factors in factorizations of a, and let L(G) be the resulting system of sets of factorization lengths. Can one determine a function f: N -> N such that, whenever |G| >= f(M), the system L(G) contains every finite set L contained in N_{>=2} whose width max L - min L is at most M?

evidence.quote: Moreover, we set L(H) = {L(a) : a ∈ H} the system of sets of lengths of H.
Problem 6.6. Can one determine a function f : N → N such that for G a finite abelian group with |G| ≥ f (M ) one has that L(G) contains each finite set L ⊂ N≥2 with max L − min L ≤ M .

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite abelian group. For each subset G0 of G whose zero-sum-sequence monoid has a nonempty distance set Delta(G0), form the minimum distance min Delta(G0), and let Delta*(G) be the set of all such minima. Does there exist a finite abelian group G for which Delta*(G) is an interval and exp(G) >= 2r(G) + 2, where r(G) is the rank of G and exp(G) is the exponent of G in its invariant-factor decomposition?

evidence.quote: We denote by r(G) = r the rank of G and by exp(G) = nr the exponent of G.
For |G| ≥ 3, one denotes by ∆∗ (G) = {min ∆(G0 ) : G0 ⊂ G, ∆(G0 ) 6= ∅}
Problem 6.21. Is there a finite abelian group G such that ∆∗ (G) is an interval and exp(G) ≥ 2r(G) + 2?

accepted.question_text: For a finite abelian group G, let B(G) be the monoid of zero-sum sequences over G and let L(G) be its system of sets of factorization lengths. The Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths for Krull monoids with finite class group says that there is a uniform bound M and a finite nonempty difference set Delta* such that each set of lengths is an almost arithmetic multiprogression with bound M and some difference d in Delta*. If D(G) denotes the Davenport constant of G, namely the supremum of lengths of minimal zero-sum sequences over G, what is the rough order of magnitude, as a function of D(G), of the uniform bound needed in this structure theorem for L(G)?

evidence.quote: The Davenport constant of G0 , denoted by D(G0 ), is defined as sup{|A| : A ∈ A(G0 )}.

Theorem 6.3. Let H be a Krull monoid with finite class group. There is some M ∈ N0 and a non-empty finite set ∆∗ ⊂ N such that for each a ∈ H its set of lengths L(a) is a AAMP with bound M and difference d in ∆∗ .
Problem 6.24. What is the (rough) order of magnitude of the bound in the STSL for L(G) (in terms of D(G))?
